rounds.text: Redington demonstrates superior operational efficiency with a ROCE of 18.4% [E12] and an ROE of 16.9% [E13], both significantly outperforming sector medians of 7.2% [E71] and 4.86% [E9] respectively, while trading at a P/E of 17.8 [E1]. This efficiency is backed by accelerating momentum, as evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth of 42% [E21] and a recent quarterly net profit surge of 94% YoY [E63]. Despite the stock sitting at its 52-week high [E48], a discounted cash flow analysis suggests a substantial margin of safety of 39.6% [E46], with an intrinsic value of Rs 679 per share compared to the current price of Rs 410 [E45]. The market's current valuation only implies a 9.1% earnings growth rate [E47], which appears conservative given the company’s 5-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E19] and its recent sales growth of 35% YoY [E61]. The business remains conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E38], maintains a healthy dividend payout of 34.8% [E59], and has seen foreign institutional holdings rise to 61.96% [E42]. Conceded: [E7], [E11], [E34], [E37], [E44], and [E53]. However, the perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51] and a rules-based buy score of 92 out of 100 [E60] suggest the market is beginning to recognize this fundamental strength.

The valuation demands intense scrutiny given that multiples trade at a premium to sector benchmarks, with a P/E of 21.11x against a sector benchmark of 18.65x and an EV/EBITDA of 12.89x compared to 10.55x [E6, E11]. Beneath these demanding multiples, a severe divergence between reported profits and actual cash generation emerges, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.18x and operating cash flow representing a mere 32% of operating profit for March 2026 [E34, E37]. This alarming disconnect where profits far outstrip cash points directly to potential risks in receivables or accruals [E34]. Compounding these fundamental cash flow concerns, the institutional sentiment shows cracks as domestic institutions reduced their holdings to 16.37% from 17.38%, and the scanX signal engine flags negative money flow alongside institutional outflow [E43, E44, E65]. Furthermore, the stock sits right at the very top of its range at 100% of its 52-week high, leaving it technically extended with a historical peak-to-trough drawdown reaching an eye-watering -80.2% [E48, E53, E66]. Conceded: the company demonstrates robust trailing sales and profit growth alongside solid return metrics [E17, E21, E12, E13].

While the bear highlights a premium P/E of 21.11x and EV/EBITDA of 12.89x against sector benchmarks [E6, E11], filed statements record a much more modest P/E of 17.8x [E1], while the business concurrently delivers a superior ROCE of 15.8% to 18.4% and an ROE of 16.9% compared to meager sector benchmarks of 6.56% and 4.86% [E8, E10, E12, E13]. Conceded: cash conversion is 0.18x and operating cash flow is 32% of operating profit for March 2026 [E34, E37], yet the company still generated positive absolute operating cash flow of Rs 231 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr alongside a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E35, E36, E38]. Although domestic institutions reduced their stake slightly [E43], foreign institutions increased their holding to 61.96% from 56.26% [E42]. Furthermore, the bear's anxiety over technical extension at the 52-week high [E48] ignores that a reverse DCF shows today's price implies only 9.1% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 16.0% [E47], while the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong 92 out of 100 on the back of explosive 35% YoY sales growth and 94% YoY net profit growth [E60, E61, E63].

Conceded: [E1] records a P/E of 17.8x, but the company still trades at a premium P/E of 21.11x and EV/EBITDA of 12.89x relative to sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. While the bull cites superior returns on capital [E8, E10, E12, E13], it glosses over the severe quality warning that cash conversion for March 2026 sits at just 0.18x, with operating cash flow representing a mere 32% of operating profit [E34, E37]. Conceded: absolute operating and free cash flows are positive [E35, E36], yet borrowings have climbed to Rs 2,842 Cr alongside a surging CWIP up 400.0% to Rs 75 Cr, which demands capital attention [E40, E41]. Furthermore, the claim of strong institutional backing ignores negative money flow with an institutional holding change of -0.28 percentage points and declining domestic institutional ownership [E43, E44, E65]. Finally, celebrating the stock sitting 100% of the way up its 52-week range [E48] disregards explicit warnings that price growth exceeds profit growth and that historical peak-to-trough drawdowns reach an alarming -80.2% [E53, E56, E57].

Conceded: [E6, E11] record higher P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples than sector benchmarks. However, the bear's valuation concern ignores the fundamental truth of intrinsic value: a discounted cash flow model explicitly pegs intrinsic value at Rs 679 per share against the market price of Rs 410, offering a substantial 39.6% margin of safety [E45, E46]. Conceded: [E34, E37] highlight weak cash conversion for March 2026, yet the business still generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 231 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36], while maintaining a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E38]. Conceded: [E43, E44, E65] point to domestic and general institutional outflows, but foreign institutional holdings actually expanded to 61.96% in June 2026 up from 56.26% in September 2023 [E42]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF proves that the current market price only prices in a modest 9.1% earnings growth rate, which is easily eclipsed by the 16.0% base case assumption and recent trailing twelve-month profit growth of 42% [E21, E47]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the company a strong BUY score of 92 out of 100, driven by powerful sales and profit expansion [E60, E61, E63].

Conceded: [E45, E46] put intrinsic value above the current price, yet the stock is running purely on price-led momentum rather than matching fundamentals, with 5-year price growth of 23% outstripping 16% profit growth and recent price gains exceeding profits by 9% [E56, E57]. Conceded: [E35, E36] show positive operating and free cash flows, but operating cash flow is a meager 32% of operating profit and cash conversion sits at just 0.18x for March 2026, signaling that profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection and require careful scrutiny of receivables [E34, E37]. Conceded: [E42] notes an increase in foreign institutional holding, but domestic institutions decreased their stake and overall institutional money flow reads negative with a holding drop of 0.28 percentage points [E43, E44, E65]. Conceded: [E21] records 42% trailing profit growth, but the 3-year profit growth has slowed to 5% and the operating margin has remained flat at 2% with an inconsistent trend over recent periods [E20, E30, E32, E33]. Finally, while the rules-based screen gives a high score [E60], the stock sits extended at 100% of its 52-year range with a severe historical drawdown risk of 80.2% and high volatility of 42.7% [E48, E53, E54, E66].
